title: Read Anyone in Seconds
description: A 60-card guided run through the body language, microexpressions, and psychology tricks that let you read anyone instantly.

cards.content: People think they hide their thoughts, but their face, body, and voice leak the truth faster than words can form.
Your brain already reads these signals subconsciously. This course just turns that instinct into a deliberate skill.
Microexpressions flash for a split second before someone can fake a smile or calm expression.
Body language is 55% of communication. Most people ignore it and wonder why they get surprised later.
Verbal cues like filler words or pitch changes reveal stress or deception in real time.
Context always matters. One signal alone can mislead you, but clusters tell the full story.
Reading people isn’t manipulation. It’s the fastest way to understand motives and protect yourself.
In conversations, the real message often hides between the lines and behind the smile.
These skills give you an unfair advantage in interviews, dates, negotiations, and everyday life.
Master this and you’ll never walk into a room wondering what someone is really thinking again.

modules.title: Microexpressions
modules.summary: The seven faces that betray everyone.

cards.content: A genuine smile crinkles the eyes. A fake one stops at the mouth. Spot the difference in a heartbeat.
Flash of contempt: one side of the lip curls up for a fraction of a second. It reveals hidden judgment.
Surprise eyebrows shoot up and stay there. If they drop too fast, the emotion is being hidden.
Fear shows in raised eyebrows and tensed lower eyelids. Watch for it when someone denies something.
Disgust wrinkles the nose and pulls the upper lip. It leaks even when someone says they’re fine.
Anger tightens the lips and lowers the brows. A micro-flash often appears right before someone lies.
Sadness pulls the inner corners of the eyebrows up. It’s the hardest to fake convincingly.
These seven universal expressions cross cultures and appear before the person can control them.
Train your eye by slowing down videos. You’ll start catching them in live conversations within days.
Once you see microexpressions, conversations become a live lie detector you carry in your head.
Crossed arms don’t always mean closed off. Context decides if it’s cold, defensive, or just comfortable.
Leaning forward signals interest. Leaning back signals doubt or a desire to escape the topic.
Feet pointing toward you show genuine engagement. Feet pointing away mean they’re mentally leaving.
Touching the neck or face often betrays anxiety or an attempt to soothe discomfort.
Open palms build trust. Hidden hands or clenched fists signal withheld information or tension.
Mirroring your movements is a subconscious sign they feel connected and safe.
Sudden stillness after fidgeting can mean someone just decided to lie or hold something back.
Legs crossed toward you indicate comfort. Crossed away creates a barrier.
Shoulders rising toward the ears signal fear or uncertainty even if the face stays neutral.
The body rarely lies when you know what to watch. Words can be chosen. Posture cannot.
Too many filler words like “um” and “like” often mean the speaker is buying time to fabricate.
Qualifiers such as “honestly” or “to be frank” frequently signal the opposite of honesty.
Repeating your question before answering is a classic stall tactic while they craft the story.
Sudden drop in vocal pitch or volume can reveal nervousness or an attempt to sound more convincing.
Over-explaining a simple answer usually means the person is trying to sell the lie harder.
Defensive phrases like “why would I do that?” often appear right before a guilty person deflects.
Speaking faster than normal can signal excitement or anxiety depending on the rest of the cluster.
Avoiding specific details and sticking to vague generalities is a red flag for deception.
A sudden change in speech pattern mid-conversation often marks the moment the truth shifts.
Words are chosen. The delivery, speed, and qualifiers are what the brain can’t rehearse.

modules.title: Cluster Reading
modules.summary: When signals line up and reveal everything.

cards.content: A single microexpression means little. Three signals together create a reliable read.
Smile plus forward lean plus open palms? Genuine interest. Smile plus crossed arms? Forced politeness.
Neck touch, foot pointing away, and vocal pitch drop together almost always mean discomfort or lying.
Baseline behavior is your reference point. Any sudden cluster of changes is the real signal.
Cultural differences matter. What looks like deception in one place is normal politeness in another.
Timing is everything. Signals that appear right after a specific question are the most telling.
When body, face, and voice all contradict the words, trust the body and face first.
Practice spotting clusters in low-stakes settings like coffee chats before high-stakes meetings.
The more clusters you catch, the less you’ll need to ask follow-up questions to know the truth.
Mastering clusters turns reading people from guesswork into a repeatable, accurate skill.

modules.title: Real-World Mastery
modules.summary: Use it daily without getting caught.

cards.content: Start every conversation by noting their baseline for thirty seconds before diving in.
Ask open questions first. People reveal more when they feel safe and talk freely.
Stay neutral with your own body language so you don’t influence or alert them.
In negotiations, watch for clusters right after you name your price or terms.
On dates, microexpressions around future plans show real excitement or hidden hesitation.
Use these skills to read the room in meetings and know exactly who is on board.
Never call someone out on a read. Just adjust your approach and keep the information private.
Daily practice on strangers in public will sharpen your eye faster than any book.
The ethical rule is simple: use it to understand, never to manipulate or harm.
Once you master this, every conversation becomes clearer, faster, and more powerful than before.
